title: Your companion is not mad, he is a clear warner.
subtitle: Think honestly about the man you have known for years
then: Qatadah reports that the Prophet ﷺ stood on As-Safa and called the clans of Quraysh one by one, warning them. Some said: {trap}this companion of yours is mad{/trap}. The verse came: do they not reflect? Ibn Kathir links it to 34:46: {idea}stand for Allah in pairs or alone, and think{/idea}.
now: Someone you have known for years, honest in everything, tells you a hard truth. Your first reaction: they have gone crazy, they are being extreme. {idea}Stop and think about who is saying it.{/idea} The person, not the label.
old: If a message makes me uncomfortable, the messenger must be unbalanced.
new: Honest reflection on the messenger's character shows the truth of the message.
try: Spend five quiet minutes alone today thinking about the life of the Prophet ﷺ, as 34:46 asks.

title: Look at the heavens, and remember your time may be near.
subtitle: Two things to look at: creation and your own deadline
then: Allah asks why people do not look at the kingdom of the heavens and earth and learn that their Maker has no equal. Ibn Kathir says they should also be warned that {trap}their lives may be near their end{/trap}. Then: {idea}in what message after this will they believe?{/idea}
now: You look up from your phone at a clear night sky, and for a second you feel very small. Then you remember the colleague who died at forty-two last spring. {idea}Both thoughts point the same way.{/idea}
old: I will get serious about faith when I am older.
new: Creation shows me Allah, and my unknown deadline tells me not to wait.
try: Tonight, step outside and look at the sky for one minute. Then make one decision you have been putting off.

title: Whom Allah leaves astray, no one else can guide.
subtitle: Wandering blindly in one's own excess

row.title: anyone else
sub: a guru, a trend, a feed

then: After asking what message people will believe if not this one, Allah says whoever He sends astray has no guide, and He leaves them {trap}wandering blindly in their transgression{/trap}. Ibn Kathir links it to 10:101: signs and warners do not benefit those who will not believe.
now: You try every self-help book, every podcast, every life coach, hoping one will finally fix you. {idea}None of them can guide a heart Allah has not opened.{/idea} Ask Him first, then the books can help.
old: The right expert or book will set me straight.
new: Guidance comes only from Allah, so I turn to Him before anyone else.
try: Before you look for advice on your next problem, make a short dua for guidance first.

title: When is the Hour? Only my Lord knows, and it comes suddenly.
subtitle: The question that matters is not when, but how ready
then: Quraysh asked the Prophet ﷺ when the Hour would come, mostly to mock it. He was told to say its knowledge is with Allah alone. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith that {trap}the Hour will come while two men have spread a cloth to trade and cannot fold it, while a man raises food to his mouth and cannot eat it{/trap}.
now: You scroll videos about end-times signs, counting which ones have happened. Meanwhile your prayers are late and your mother is waiting for a call. {idea}The Hour comes suddenly, mid-errand.{/idea} Readiness is today's work.
old: If I knew when, I would prepare.
new: Not knowing when is the reason to be ready now.
try: Ask yourself: if it came during my next ordinary task, would I be at peace? Fix one thing.

title: If I knew the unseen, I would have avoided all harm.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say he does not know the future

row.title: no power
sub: over my own harm or benefit

row.title: no unseen
sub: or I would have avoided loss

row.title: Allah alone
sub: even the Prophet ﷺ said so

then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to say he has no power over benefit or harm to himself, except as Allah wills. Ibn 'Abbas explained: {idea}if I knew the unseen, I would know which deals would profit, and poverty would never touch me{/idea}. He is only a warner and a bringer of good news.
now: Someone offers to read your future in a cup, a palm, an app. You are anxious about the job interview, the test results. {idea}If even the Prophet ﷺ did not know the unseen, no one at a market stall does.{/idea}
old: Someone might be able to tell me what is coming.
new: The unseen is with Allah alone, so I trust Him and prepare.
try: When anxious about the future today, say: Allah knows and I do not, and do one practical thing.

title: Expecting a child, they both turned to Allah.
subtitle: Spouses made for rest, and a prayer for a good child
then: Allah created people from one soul and made its mate from it, so that each finds rest in the other. Ibn Kathir cites 30:21: {reward}He put between you affection and mercy{/reward}. As the pregnancy grows heavy, the couple both pray: if You give us a good child, {idea}we will be among the grateful{/idea}.
now: The ultrasound appointment. Both of you holding hands, saying ya Allah, let everything be okay. {idea}Fear brings couples to their knees together.{/idea} The promise you make there matters.
old: Once the baby is healthy, the worrying is over.
new: The gratitude I promise in fear is what Allah watches for after the gift.
try: If you have a spouse or child, thank Allah for them by name tonight, out loud.

title: When He gave the gift, they gave others the credit.
subtitle: Forgetting the Giver once the child arrives
then: When Allah gave them a good child, {trap}they ascribed partners to Him in what He gave{/trap}. Ibn Kathir prefers Al-Hasan's view: this is not about Adam and Hawwa', but about later people who did this. The verse moves from the first pair to humanity in general.
now: The baby is born healthy. Someone says it was the lucky bracelet, the special diet, the great hospital. The doctors deserve thanks. {idea}But the gift came from Allah.{/idea} The first thanks belongs to Him.
old: Things worked out because of what we did.
new: I thank people for their part, but the gift itself is from Allah alone.
try: Think of one answered prayer. Thank Allah for it first, then thank the people who helped.

title: They worship what creates nothing and was itself created.
subtitle: A simple test for anything you treat as ultimate
then: Allah asks how people can associate with Him things that create nothing and are themselves created. Ibn Kathir cites 22:73: {trap}all the false gods together could not create a fly{/trap}, and if a fly took something from them, they could not get it back.
now: Your career, your brand, your bank balance. You made them, or someone else did. {trap}None of them can create even a fly.{/trap} Yet some mornings they decide whether you feel worth anything.
old: What I have built is what gives my life meaning.
new: Only the Creator deserves my devotion, not anything created.
try: Watch a small insect for a minute today. Remember no human power could make it.

title: They cannot help their worshippers, or even themselves.
subtitle: The idol that could not defend itself
then: Ibn Kathir tells of 'Amr bin Al-Jamuh, whose idol two young Companions kept overturning at night. He left a sword by it and said: defend yourself. When it was found tied to a dead dog, he said: {trap}had you been a god, you would not end up like this{/trap}. He embraced Islam and was later martyred at Uhud.
now: You count on your contacts, your savings, your reputation to protect you. Then a rumor spreads, or the market drops, and they cannot even save themselves. {idea}Rely on what cannot fall.{/idea}
old: What I lean on will hold me up when trouble comes.
new: Anything that cannot protect itself cannot protect me.
try: Name the one thing you lean on most besides Allah. Say: Hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.

title: Call them to guidance or stay silent, it is the same.
subtitle: The idols cannot hear or follow
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the idols do not hear those who call them, so calling them or ignoring them makes no difference. He cites Ibrahim's words to his father in 19:42: {trap}why do you worship what neither hears nor sees nor helps you at all?{/trap}
now: You pour your worries into a group chat, a diary, a playlist at 3am. Nothing answers back. {idea}Allah is As-Sami', the One who hears{/idea}, even what you have not said out loud.
old: Talking it out anywhere will make me feel better.
new: The One who truly hears is Allah, so I bring my worries to Him first.
try: Tonight, before telling anyone else about a worry, tell Allah in dua.

title: What you call on besides Allah are servants like you.
subtitle: Created things cannot answer prayer
then: Allah tells the idol worshippers that those they call on are servants like themselves. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}the worshipper is better than the idol{/idea}, for the worshipper at least hears, sees and has strength. The verse challenges them: call on them and let them answer.
now: You keep checking for a message from the one person you think can fix your situation: a manager, an ex, a relative with connections. {trap}They are servants like you{/trap}, as needy as you. {idea}Ask the One they all depend on.{/idea}
old: The right person can solve this for me.
new: People are servants like me, so I ask their Master first.
try: Before asking anyone for a big favor this week, ask Allah for it in two rak'ahs.

title: Do they have feet, hands, eyes or ears? Then plot, and wait.
subtitle: The Prophet's ﷺ fearless challenge
then: The verse asks whether the idols have feet, hands, eyes or ears. Then the Prophet ﷺ is told to say: call your partners, plot against me, and {idea}give me no respite{/idea}. Ibn Kathir compares it to Hud's words in 11:54-56: {reward}I put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord{/reward}.
now: You are afraid of the evil eye, a curse, a superstition about the wrong day to travel. {idea}They have no hands to touch you without Allah's leave.{/idea} Say your adhkar and walk out the door with calm.
old: I need to be careful not to anger unseen powers.
new: Nothing harms me without Allah's permission, so I trust Him and stop fearing.
try: Say the morning adhkar today, then let go of one superstition you have been holding.
